title: Gradle / JUnit support, so Kotlin and Android projects get real red proofs
description: The kernel recognised Kotlin and Java files but had no Gradle runner: failing test names could not be parsed, so every red proof on a Kotlin project degraded to exit-code-only evidence, and JUnit skip annotations were invisible to the integrity leg.

clauses.text: Failing test names are extracted from Gradle's console output, and Gradle's own task and build failure lines are never mistaken for tests.
clauses.observable_by: extractForRunner('gradle', captured) returns exactly the two failing tests in a captured run that also contains '> Task ... FAILED' and 'BUILD FAILED'

clauses.text: JUnit skip annotations in Kotlin and Java tests are reported by the integrity leg.
clauses.observable_by: a Kotlin test with @Ignore and a Java test with @Disabled each count as skipped

clauses.text: A Gradle project is detected and its unit tests run through the project's own wrapper; without a wrapper, no command is guessed.
clauses.observable_by: detectStack returns stack gradle with ./gradlew test (testDebugUnitTest for Android), and an empty gate when gradlew is absent

cases.description: Gradle failing names extracted, task/build lines excluded
cases.test_name: gate extracts gradle failing test names and ignores task and build lines
integrity finds JUnit skips in Kotlin and Java tests

cases.description: gradle detected, wrapper used, Android gets testDebugUnitTest
cases.test_name: detects a gradle project and runs its unit tests through the wrapper
a gradle build with no wrapper resolves no gate rather than guessing a global gradle

non_goals: Assertion-free detection for Kotlin test bodies; the declaration slicer is JS/Python-shaped and extending it is separate work.
Parsing JUnit XML reports; the console format is what the gate already captures.
